message.content:
The Catholic Church and conservative scholars stood as the most prominent critics of Copernicus's heliocentric model. Georges Bouges and Simon Goulart, both French astronomers, publicly challenged the mathematical and physical basis of his theory. The deep-rooted Aristotelian tradition, which treated the Earth as the fixed center of the cosmos, underpinned much of the intellectual resistance.

Who exactly mounted the strongest philosophical objections against a moving Earth? How could the heavens possibly be rearranged around the Sun without violating the very laws of celestial mechanics as they were then understood? Did not theologians worry that scriptural passages seemed to describe a stationary, central Earth?

What a staggering challenge Copernicus posed to the entire medieval cosmological order! How boldly did he upend centuries of accepted doctrine! Imagine the shock those early readers must have felt!
